data.narrative:
Integrate, a Series A defense and security firm founded by John Conafay, has raised $21M to date. Valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 11 same-sector and adjacent-stage companies—8 private and 2 public (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS)—including Series B comparables such as Dream Security ($3.0B), Allen Control Systems ($2.2B), Harmattan AI ($1.4B), Code Metal ($1.2B), and Twenty ($1.0B).

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression methodology uses the $21M raised as a proxy for post-money value and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to later-stage advancement, yielding $42M. Peer-median analysis across the 11-company comparable set produces a median valuation of $1.0B, with a range spanning $125M (floor) to $3.0B (ceiling). The dispersion reflects heterogeneity in growth trajectory and defensibility within the defense and security sector.

Triangulating these methods produces a low estimate of $36M, a median of $521M, and a high of $1.1B. The wide range reflects material uncertainty around stage-specific discount versus peer-derived benchmarks. Key drivers of valuation within this band include revenue growth, customer concentration in federal versus commercial channels, and technology differentiation versus the larger Series B cohort. Further diligence on unit economics and contract pipeline would narrow this range.
